chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in the Muhrim (person in Ihram) entering the bathhouse, but he should not scrub his body."
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And he should not trim his nails.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يَتَدَلَّكُ: To scrub or rub the body vigorously (removing skin/dirt)

ai.seo_question: What are the restrictions on bathing and grooming for a Muhrim during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the reliable chain of Fadala ibn Ayub, clarifies that the prohibition for the Muhrim is not merely physical presence in the bathhouse but specifically the act of vigorous scrubbing (tadalluk) to remove skin, which is considered a form of grooming. Shaykh al-Tusi adds the trimming of nails to this list, establishing a consistent jurisprudential principle that minor grooming acts are prohibited to maintain the distinct state of Ihram. This highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving the spiritual simplicity and uniformity of the pilgrim during the sacred rites.
